issue.question: Does the finite-nuisance quotient preserve nuisance-span removal and estimability under changes of parameter units?
issue.exact_missing_or_defect: Valid equivalent normal equations can silently retain an included nuisance mean; scaling a wholly nonestimable contrast can also convert its null estimate into a reported identified zero.
issue.risk: The adapter can report biased, apparently estimable physical contrasts despite unchanged nuisance span or exact nonidentifiability.

findings.title: Raw Gram eigenvalue truncation silently removes valid nuisance directions after unit changes
findings.reproduction: D=[[1,0],[0,1],[0,0],[0,0]], H=[[1,0],[0,0],[1,0],[0,1]], y=D@[1,2]+H@[10,20]. With X=[D,H], the adapter returns [1,2]. With X=[D,H@diag(1e-6,1)] and unchanged y, it returns [11,2], with both contrasts marked estimable. Both inputs are exact valid normal equations and have the same nuisance span.

findings.title: Absolute contrast tolerance promotes a scaled nonestimable contrast to an identified zero
findings.reproduction: Use X=[[1,0,1],[0,1,0]], signal_dim=2 and y=[3,4]. K=[[1,0]] correctly returns contrast_estimable=false and estimate=null. K=[[1e-8,0]] incorrectly returns true and estimate=0, although multiplying a nonzero contrast by a scalar cannot change estimability.

findings.title: Reported six-contrast eigenvalue range does not match generated result
findings.reproduction: Report gives4.18670e-5 to0.00170770. Generated low-minus-high/middle-minus-high basis gives2.2573001869759178e-5 to0.0033602163628226414.
